general_information.Time Allocation: 150h = 45h contact hours (60 sessions) + 0.75h final exam + 50h guided practice (5h x 10 days) + 54.25h self-study.
general_information.Description: -Objective: To help students to apply learned knowledge and skills of tour guide to the fieldtrip that the class and lecturer will build up together; to develop the ability to evaluate effectively a tour program and practice the profession of tour guide. -Description: The course focuses on the practical steps of: preparation before welcoming guests; building a professional image and attitude; work when receiving group documents; procedures for welcoming and dropping off guests; check-in procedures at hotels, restaurants, tourist attractions, airports, customs; skills in acquiring knowledge and conveying it to tourists; ability to observe and judge tourists' psychology; how to handle situations when going on a tour. The course also emphasizes the responsibility and ability to work under pressure of a tour guide. The course determines cheerleading skills, teambuilding skills, organizing games. The course guides students to prepare presentation on various themes. Teaching method is to review theoretical knowledge from the subject TTG311 and practice tasks in a practical way by assigning roles to perform tour guide work on a simulated bus or field trip, etc.
general_information.StudentTasks: Students must attend at least 80% of contact slots in order to be accepted to the final examination. Students must attend the whole fieldtrip in order to pass this course. Student is responsible to do all distributed tasks, practical assignments given by instructor in class and on site, also submit on time the final report. Use laptop in class only for learning purpose Promptly access to http://flm.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Carry out the process of receiving a tour from the company and clearly define the tasks and responsibilities of the tour guide during the trip.
List and perform the necessary preparations before the tour begins and during tour.
Practice airport procedures: assisting guests with check-in, baggage handling, and guiding them through security checkpoints.
Apply knowledge in real-life settings at hotels, restaurants, and tourist attractions: handling check-ins, meal orders, and sightseeing guidance.
Practice presentation and public speaking skills when introducing information to guests throughout the tour.
Practice designing team building programs, gala dinners, and conference coordination
Apply skills to handle real-life situations on tour.
Take notes, evaluate the tour experience, and reflect for continuous improvement in future trips.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Practice tour guide tasks in team.
assessments.Grading Guide: Choose 1 of the 2 following tasks: (Or the instructor has other options suitable for the subject's reality). Practical Task 1: Team Building and Group Engagement Activities Students will be divided into groups and assigned to organize team-building sessions, mini games, or other forms of group engagement activities aimed at enhancing group cohesion and participant morale. Assessment Criteria (suggested): • Planning and program design • Budgeting and cost-effectiveness • Creativity and engagement level • Effectiveness of implementation All activities must be planned and executed within a budget framework approved by the lecturer. Assessment Deliverables: Program outline, budget plan, and implementation session (may be conducted in class or in the field, as directed by the lecturer). Practical Task 2: Tour Design and Costing Student groups are required to design a comprehensive tour program lasting 5 to 7 days, based on parameters specified by the lecturer (such as travel duration, route, number of tourists, and target market segment). Required Components: • Detailed tour itinerary and included/excluded services • List of recommended restaurants and accommodation providers • Accommodation and dining arrangements aligned with the needs of the target customers • Complete pricing structure matching the listed services • Presentation of the tour package Assessment Criteria (suggested): • Relevance and logic of the itinerary in relation to duration and target audience • Appropriateness of selected services (accommodation, dining, attractions) • Consistency and accuracy of cost estimates • Quality of presentation and supporting materials Assessment Deliverables: Written tour program, price quotation, service provider list (restaurants and hotels), and a group presentation. The lecturer may also apply alternative forms of evaluation depending on instructional goals.
assessments.Note: Instruction and schedules for fieldtrips/games program and assignments must be presented in the Course Implementation Progress test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has resposibility to review, analyze and evaluate the performance for students after graded.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Practice some tour guide tasks learned in theory in this course.
assessments.Grading Guide: Option 1: Guided Practical Assignments As part of the course requirements, students are expected to engage in a series of guided practical exercises simulating the responsibilities of a professional tour guide. The following activities are compulsory: • Practical Task 1: Simulated check-in and check-out procedures conducted at the school’s training hotel facility. • Practical Task 2: Formal welcome of a tour group and introductory presentation of selected tourist attractions as assigned by the instructor. • Practical Task 3: Delivery of guided commentary at designated tourist sites, including group farewell and formal tour conclusion procedures. • Practical Task 4: Application of problem-solving skills through scenario-based exercises, reflecting real-life challenges faced by tour guides (as provided by the instructor). Option 2: Additionally, based on practical circumstances, the instructor reserves the right to assign and evaluate individual exercises as part of the course assessment.
assessments.Note: Instruction and schedules for fieldtrips and assignments must be presented in the Course Implementation Progress test must be taken right after the last lectures of required material. Instructor has resposibility to review, analyze and evaluate the performance for students after graded.
